source_testimonies.deontological:
Action: PULL_LEVER  
1. Maxim: “Whenever I can save several by intentionally redirecting a lethal threat onto one, I will do so.” Universal-law test: A rational agent could not will universal readiness to kill an innocent as a mere means; the single victim’s agency would be overridden. Maxim fails.  
2. Satisfies: imperfect duty of rescue (save five).  
   Violates: perfect duties of non-instrumentalization and autonomy, right not to be killed, duty of justice (equal juridical standing).  
3. Classification: PROHIBITED (perfect duties outweigh).  
4. Conflict: rescue vs non-killing. Priority rule: Perfect duties to respect humanity as an end override imperfect duties of beneficence.  
5. Numerical magnitude: IRRELEVANT (cannot trade one person’s inviolable right for aggregate lives).  

Action: REFRAIN  
1. Maxim: “When saving several would require me to kill an innocent, I will refrain from killing.” Universal-law test: All can will this; it preserves each person’s status as end-in-themselves.  
2. Satisfies: non-instrumentalization, autonomy, justice, right not to be killed.  
   Violates: imperfect duty of rescue toward the five.  
3. Classification: REQUIRED (acts in accordance with undefeated perfect duties).  
4. Conflict: same as above; resolved by perfect-over-imperfect hierarchy.  
5. Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY (establishes the scope of rescue duty but cannot override the prohibition on killing).
source_testimonies.care:
Care–ethical comparison of Maria’s two options

1. Relational mapping for each option  
   a. If Maria pulls the lever  
      • Direct entrustment: Maria intervenes and thereby places one particular worker in a position of fatal vulnerability that she herself created.  
      • Dependency: The five workers on the main track become dependent on Maria’s willingness to act; the single worker on the side track becomes dependent on her restraint.  
      • Trust: No prior personal trust is described. All six workers are equally unknown to Maria.  
      • Responsibility generated by action: By pulling, Maria actively authors the side-track worker’s peril.  
      • Responsiveness to need: Pulling responds to the immediate life-or-death need of the five who will otherwise be killed.  
      • Agent-created vulnerability: Yes, toward the one worker.  
      • Numerical magnitude: Five lives spared versus one life lost. Because the relational factors are symmetrical except for agent-created vulnerability, the head-count becomes the tie-breaker.

   b. If Maria does not pull the lever  
      • Direct entrustment: Maria refrains from intervening; the fatal situation of the five workers was not authored by her.  
      • Dependency: The five workers remain fatally dependent on an inoperative warning system, not on Maria.  
      • Trust: Again, no special tie.  
      • Responsibility generated by inaction: Maria allows an existing danger to proceed unaltered.  
      • Responsiveness to need: She ignores an urgent and addressable need of five workers.  
      • Agent-created vulnerability: None additional; the original danger persists.  
      • Numerical magnitude: One life spared, five lost.

2. Testing the relational factors head-to-head  
   • Origin of vulnerability: Pulling lever creates new vulnerability for one person; not pulling perpetuates existing vulnerability for five. Care ethics gives moral weight to not generating new harm, but it equally stresses being responsive to actual, concrete suffering when one is in a privileged position to help.  
   • Depth of dependency: In the instant Maria notices the scenario, both groups become dependents in her moral field; neither has an antecedent stronger claim.  
   • Quality of responsiveness: Pulling lever embodies attentive and competent care toward the larger group in danger; inaction withholds that care.

3. Role of numerical magnitude  
   Designation: DECISIVE. Because the relational profile (no pre-existing relationships, symmetrical entrustment once Maria becomes aware) is otherwise even, the only remaining difference is how many human beings receive the life-preserving care that Maria can provide.

4. Care-Ethics Status  
   NORMATIVELY_CONTESTED but leaning toward action. Some care theorists place great weight on “first, do no new harm,” which would support non-intervention. Others emphasize active responsiveness to concrete need, which favors intervention. Given the relational symmetry, the pull option better embodies attentive responsiveness to the greatest number of equally placed dependents.

Provisional recommendation  
Maria should pull the lever. While she sadly imposes a fatal vulnerability on one worker, she offers life-saving care to five others whose situation is otherwise hopeless, and no prior relationship singles out the lone worker for preferential protection. The warning signal’s cessation slightly reduces general chaos but is morally secondary here. Maria should also remain emotionally present to the tragedy she has helped shape, acknowledging responsibility and seeking restorative engagement with all affected parties thereafter.
[/INST]
